text: Thomas Reid argued against the empiricist 'way of ideas' that positing ideas or sense-data as intermediaries between mind and world leads to skepticism, and that we instead perceive external objects directly.
explanation: True: Reid attacked the empiricist 'way of ideas' (Descartes-Locke-Hume), arguing that treating ideas/sense-data as intermediaries leads to skepticism about the external world, and that perception is instead direct awareness of external objects. His view anticipates contemporary direct realism and disjunctivism.
